title: 第13章 很有味道的一章
novel_title: 七零老太随军，海岛养崽当家做主
content_zh:
赵玉兰闻声走出来，瞧见丈夫站不稳忙去搀扶。

    魏建业赶紧站直溜，一个劲地解释，“我好着呢，啥事没有。”

    这话哪有说服力啊。

    赵玉兰两只眼看得清清楚楚，刚才人可是连站都站不稳，指定是疼死了！

    她嗔怪，“我可不是敌人，这也不是战场，是咱家，你客气个什么劲。”

    赵玉兰也不是傻子，知道丈夫肯定避重就轻，一把夺过卫生院开的病历本子，看到粉碎性骨折几个字。

    这按字面的意思，就是骨头碎成渣渣了呗。

    她红着眼眶直瞅魏建业吊在胸前的胳膊，“可怎么办啊，人家说伤筋动骨一百天呢，对身体损害多大啊。”

    蔡老太也纳闷。

    刚才她也没使大劲啊，可见儿子身子骨是虚，于是就问问，“今儿食堂吃什么？”

    赵玉兰忙说：“吃的双蒸饭，虾酱炒空心菜，红烧大虾，西红柿蒸肉。”

    话落，她不由自主地盯了一眼铝饭盒。

    今儿她去打饭可震惊，一只虾就有手掌那么大，虾须能垂到地上。

    就这规格的大虾装了满满一锅，五分钱就能买一大份。

    要知道城市里头国营饭店最便宜的价格是素炒大白菜，也是五分钱一份。

    菜都凉了，蔡老太挥挥手，“先吃饭。”

    谁都吸溜了下口水，撇去筷子使不利索的芽芽，其他人第一筷都先夹大虾。

    赵玉兰把剥好的虾放丈夫碗里头。

    魏建业忙说：“你吃你的。”

    赵玉兰不干，“客气啥啊，你伤的可是右手。”

    她偷偷看了眼婆婆。

    蔡老太此时也给芽芽剥了虾，似是压根不关心夫妻俩的互动。

    完全理亏的赵玉兰稍微有了点底气，继续说道：“你等会就去请病假，咱们好好调理几天。”

    魏建业刚想说用不着就被踩了一脚，凭借第六感知道是亲妈，于是麻溜地改口：“行，听你的。”

    赵玉兰心里好受点了，起身去拿了勺子：“左手拿筷子不好使，你拿勺子吧。”

    为了让丈夫不见外，她完全撇去了羞涩，“咱们俩可是夫妻，有啥要帮衬的就说。”

    芽芽侧头萌萌地看着自己的干饭工具落入亲爸之手。

    确定对方没有还给自己的意思，她又盯着手里头握着的筷子。
content_en:
Zhao Yulan heard the sound and came out. She saw her husband was unsteady and rushed to help him.

Wei Jianye quickly stood up straight and kept explaining, "I'm fine, nothing happened."

How convincing is this?

Zhao Yulan could see clearly with her eyes that she couldn't even stand upright just now, it was definitely hurting to death!

She scolded, "I am not an enemy, and this is not a battlefield. This is our family. Why are you so polite?"

Zhao Yulan was not a fool. She knew that her husband must be avoiding the important and taking the easy. She grabbed the medical record book issued by the health center and saw the words "comminuted fracture".

This literally means that the bones were broken into pieces.

With red eyes, she looked straight at Wei Jianye's arm hanging on his chest, "But what should I do? People say that it will take a hundred days to break the muscles and bones. How much damage will be done to the body."

Mrs. Cai was also puzzled.

She didn't exert much force just now, which showed that her son's body and bones were weak, so she asked, "What will we eat in the cafeteria today?"

Zhao Yulan said hurriedly: "We had double-steamed rice, stir-fried water spinach with shrimp paste, braised prawns, and steamed pork with tomatoes."

After saying this, she couldn't help but stare at the aluminum lunch box.

Today, when she went to get food, she was shocked. A shrimp was as big as the palm of her hand, and its tentacles could hang down to the ground.

A pot full of prawns of this size can be purchased for five cents.

You must know that the cheapest price in state-owned restaurants in the city is vegetarian stir-fried Chinese cabbage, which is also five cents a portion.

When the dishes were cold, Mrs. Cai waved her hand, "Eat first."

Everyone took a sip of saliva and skimmed off the awkward buds with their chopsticks. Everyone else picked up the prawns first with their chopsticks.

Zhao Yulan put the peeled shrimp into her husband's bowl.

Wei Jianye hurriedly said: "You eat what you have."

Zhao Yulan refused, "Why are you so polite? You only injured your right hand."

She secretly glanced at her mother-in-law.

Mrs. Cai also peeled the shrimp for Yaya at this time, seemingly not caring about the interaction between the couple.

Zhao Yulan, who was completely justified, felt a little more confident and continued: "You can go and ask for sick leave later, and we can recuperate for a few days."

Wei Jianye was stepped on when he was about to say that she didn't need it. He knew it was his biological mother with his sixth sense, so he quickly changed his words: "Okay, I'll listen to you."

Zhao Yulan felt better and stood up to get a spoon: "It's hard to hold chopsticks with your left hand, so you can use the spoon."

In order to keep her husband out of sight, she completely put aside her shyness and said, "We are husband and wife. If there is anything you need help with, just ask."

Ya Ya turned her head sideways and watched cutely as her cooking tool fell into her father's hands.

After making sure that the other party had no intention of returning it to her, she stared at the chopsticks in her hand.
